The '''2019–20 season''' was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s 106th competitive season, 31st consecutive season in the top flight of English football, 28th consecutive season in the [[Premier League]], and 114th year in existence as a football club.<ref>{{Cite web|title=History|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/about-chelsea/history|website=chelseafc.com|date=1 July 2019}}</ref> The season was slated to cover the period from 1 July 2019 to 30 June 2020, but due to the suspension of football due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe|COVID-19 pandemic]], it was extended to 8 August 2020.

The season was the first since [[2011–12 Chelsea F.C. season|2011–12]] without [[Eden Hazard]], who departed to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=7 June 2019|title=Eden Hazard: Real Madrid sign Chelsea forward for fee that could exceed £150m|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48548361|access-date=30 March 2021}}</ref>

On 16 June 2019, manager [[Maurizio Sarri]] departed Chelsea, signing for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48633265|title=Maurizio Sarri: Juventus appoint Chelsea manager|access-date=31 December 2023|date=16 June 2019|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 4 July, former player [[Frank Lampard]] signed on a three-year contract, replacing Sarri as head coach.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/07/04/frank-lampard-returns-to-chelsea |title=Frank Lampard returns to Chelsea |publisher=Chelsea Football Club |date=4 July 2019 |access-date=31 December 2023}}</ref>
